translationRepairs: He came from Jieqiu in Taiyuan commandery.
He came from Jiexiu in Taiyuan commandery.
界休 is Jiexiu (休 = xiu); Jieqiu misreads the graph. The following note 介休 confirms the same place.
He was a man of Jieqiu in Taiyuan commandery.
He was a man of Jiexiu in Taiyuan commandery.
The literal line repeats the same misreading of 界休 as Jieqiu; Jiexiu is the correct romanization.
The commentary names 介休, modern Jiexiu, not Jieqiu.
The literal line likewise writes Jieqiu for 介休; Jiexiu is required.
When he first met Commandant of Henan Li Ying, Ying thought him extraordinary; they became close friends, and thereafter his name shook the capital.
When he first met Governor of Henan Li Ying, Ying thought him extraordinary; they became close friends, and thereafter his name shook the capital.
河南尹 is the metropolitan governor (yin) of Henan, not a commandant. The idiomatic line already has governor.
Liu Xiang's Xin Xu tells how Marquis Wen of Wei bowed from his chariot at Duan Ganmu's lane, granted him a vast stipend, and called on him often.
The Xin Xu tells how Marquis Wen of Wei bowed from his chariot at Duan Ganmu's lane, granted him a vast stipend, and called on him often.
This unit cites only 《新序》; Liu Xiang is not named and should not be invented here.
When Qin planned to strike Wei, Sima Tang objected: "Everyone knows Wei honors the worthy Duan Ganmu—surely this is no time to march."』
When Qin planned to strike Wei, Sima Tang objected: "Duan Ganmu is a worthy man, and Wei treats him with ceremony—the whole world has heard of it; is it not perhaps impermissible to apply arms?"
The remonstrance is 段干木賢者也，而魏禮之，天下莫不聞，無乃不可加兵乎; 'no time to march' drops worthiness, ritual honor, and the rhetorical 'is it not perhaps impermissible to apply arms.'
〈(The Analects: Qu Boyu's messenger asks Confucius's disciple, 『What has the Master been up to?』
〈(The Analects: Qu Boyu sent a man to Confucius, who asked him, 『What has the Master been doing?』
蘧伯玉使人於孔子，問之曰 has Qu Boyu send someone to Confucius, who then asks about the Master; the original wrongly has the messenger question a disciple.
He answered: "To heap scorn on the unworthy only deepens the trouble—that is what Confucius meant."
He answered: "If a person is not humane, to hate him to excess is to bring disorder."
s0099 quotes 人而不仁，疾之以甚，亂也 without naming Confucius; 'that is what Confucius meant' is supplied from the next note and is not in this unit.
He won a reputation for stern integrity, entered the central administration, rose to attendant censor and governor of Bing, and left a record of moral sway wherever he served.
He won a reputation for stern integrity, entered the central administration, rose to attendant censor and inspector of Bing, and left a record of moral sway wherever he served.
并州刺史 is provincial inspector (cishi), not a commandery governor (taishou).
〈(Xie Cheng: "Jia Shu had avenged his uncle Song Yuan in town, been arrested, and faced the death cell—
〈(Xie Cheng: "Jia Shu had avenged his maternal uncle Song Yuan in town, been arrested, and faced the death cell—
舅 is the maternal uncle; generic 'uncle' erases the maternal line named in 淑爲舅宋瑗報讎.
Xie Zhen (distinct from the historian Xie Cheng), courtesy name Ziwei, hailed from Shaoling in Runan.
Xie Zhen, courtesy name Ziwei, hailed from Shaoling in Runan.
The Chinese is only 謝甄字子微，汝南召陵人也; the parenthetical contrast with historian Xie Cheng is not in the source.

Li Ying received Guo Tai with the rites due to a teacher and friend, and Guo's reputation shook the realm—that was Fu Rong's doing.")〉
待以師友之禮 is the rites due to a teacher and friend, not reception as 'equal and mentor.'
Rong went once and recommended and advanced three commandery scholars—Fan Ran, Han Zhuo, Kong Zhou, and others,
Rong went once and recommended and advanced three commandery scholars—Fan Ran, Han Zhuo, and Kong Zhou.
范冉、韓卓、孔伷等三人 names exactly those three men; 'and others' invents further people.
Xu Shao's kinsmen Xu Jing, Xu Xun, and Xu Xiang had all reached the three highest posts; Xu Xiang had curried favor with the eunuchs to get there and repeatedly summoned Xu Shao to court.

Xu Shao's great-uncle Jing, Jing's son Xun, and Xun's son Xiang had all reached the three highest posts; Xiang, because he could flatter the eunuchs, reached the high offices and was enfeoffed as a marquis, and repeatedly sent to invite Shao.
劭從祖敬，敬子訓，訓子相 is great-uncle Jing, his son Xun, and Xun's son Xiang, all 三公; 自致台司封侯 and 數遣請劭 also require the enfeoffment and invitations the original dropped.
He spurned Minister Yang Biao, the recommendations for upright and plain virtue, and imperial summons.
The Minister of Works Yang Biao summoned him; he was recommended for upright and plain virtue and received an imperial summons, but he accepted none of these.
司空楊彪辟 is Yang Biao (Minister of Works) summoning Xu Shao, not Shao spurning Yang; 舉方正、敦樸，徵，皆不就 covers the recommendations and imperial summons together.
When Sun Ce pacified Wu, Shao and Yao fled south to Yuzhang and died; he was forty-six years old at the time.
When Sun Ce pacified Wu, Shao fled south to Yuzhang with Yao and died; he was forty-six years old at the time.
劭與繇南奔豫章而卒，時年四十六: both flee, but 而卒 and the age belong to the biography's subject Shao, not jointly to Yao.
